coupling: The earlier CPIX commit adds an optional caller-provided output buffer to the base64 decoder; existing callers still pass NULL, so decoding allocates owned storage. The later XML-text commit avoids copying text and, for multiline PlainValue data, offers that parser-owned text as the output buffer. Without the earlier edit the offer is ignored and decoding allocates; without the later edit the decoder receives no offered buffer. Together, decoding returns parser-owned storage and the existing gf_free(decoded) frees it before DOM destruction uses and frees it again. A correct repair must align the decoder output ownership rule with the caller and XML parser lifetimes across both commits.
